summary: Regional latency spike causing timeouts for eu-west and ap-southeast customers (cross-region routing suspected)
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in eu-west and ap-southeast observed large increases in inference latency and intermittent request timeouts for text-generation endpoints starting ~2026-03-03T09:15Z. Affected traffic appears to be routed cross-region (requests from EU routed to us-east) which increases tail latency and causes timeouts for bursty workloads.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints experiencing 500ms -> 3s median latency increase and tail latencies up to 12s for some requests.
- Several timeouts observed and customer reports increased 5xx errors.
- Affects enterprise and dedicated customers with eu-west and ap-southeast preference.

Environment:
- prod (global)
- Affected regions: eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (requests being routed to us-east-1)

Observed behavior:
- Requests originating in eu-west/ap-southeast are occasionally routed to us-east backend pools.
- Streaming connections sometimes break after long TCP handshake / upstream selection delays.

Expected behavior:
- Requests should be routed to nearest healthy region per routing policy. Latency should remain within SLOs (~<300ms for short completions).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send concurrent text-generation requests (n=50) pinned to model "redwood/gpt-70b-stream" with region preference set to eu-west.
2) Observe increased request latencies and occasional 504/500s.
3) Check request trace to see selected backend region.

Relevant logs / traces / links:
- Sample trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/abcd-2026-03-03-eu-us-route
- API gateway access logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/gateway/2026-03-03/eu-west-request-samples.log
- Relevant Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234SUPPORT/p1677930000000
steps_to_reproduce: Send 50 concurrent generation requests from eu-west with region preference eu-west and no region pinning
Observe request selection in traces and latency in gateway logs
Run curl to /v1/health on selected backend to verify perceived region
logs: Gateway log excerpts show X-Selected-Region: us-east-1 for requests with source_ip in eu-west
LB health-check flapping events around 2026-03-03T09:12Z in eu-west pool
Increased DNS TTL expiry and fallback selection in GSLB logs at 2026-03-03T09:10Z
investigation_notes: 09:25 UTC - Initial triage by Support: confirmed customer-reported latency spikes and timeouts. Mitigated impact for NimbleHealth by recommending region pinning as temporary workaround.
09:40 UTC - Observed that GSLB started serving fallback records with lower geographic affinity after a config push at ~09:08Z (config change ID cfg-2026-03-03-11).
10:05 UTC - API-gateway metrics show increased upstream selection time and a higher percentage of upstreams selected in us-east for eu-west source IPs.
10:35 UTC - SRE reproduced cross-region routing by triggering DNS expiry; route selection favored us-east pool due to a weight misconfiguration in rollout rule 'gslb-weight-v2'.
11:10 UTC - Hypothesis: recent rollout of gslb-weight-v2 unintentionally reduced geo-affinity in presence of transient health-check flaps, causing more cross-region fallbacks.
11:40 UTC - Validated by comparing request traces pre/post change: confirmed significant uptick in X-Selected-Region mismatch coincident with rollout timestamp.

12:00 UTC - Quick rollback of gslb-weight-v2 performed (PR: https://github.com/redwood/gslb-configs/pull/1123) which restored expected geo-affinity in canary region. Observed client latency returning toward baseline in eu-west.
13:15 UTC - Follow-up: created INT-412 for a full postmortem and to add stricter rollout guardrails and automated canary checks for geo-affinity metrics.
comments: Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-03T09:30Z: Reached out to customer to acknowledge the issue and provided temporary guidance to pin region in client headers. Asked for recent request IDs.
Customer (NimbleHealth - Priya Singh) 2026-03-03T09:45Z: Provided request IDs and noted timeouts around 09:15-09:35 UTC. Reported that this started after a routine maintenance window.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-03T10:10Z: Investigating GSLB rollout and LB health-check behavior. Will validate rollout logs and consider rollback if geo-affinity is impacted.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-03T12:05Z: Performed rollback of gslb-weight-v2 roll-out; monitoring latency and routing metrics. Asking Support to confirm customer impact now.
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-03T12:20Z: Customer reports latency reduced to expected levels after rollback. Will keep ticket open for postmortem and follow-up tasks.
resolution_notes: Root cause: a GSLB rollout (gslb-weight-v2) reduced geo-affinity in the presence of transient health-check flapping, increasing cross-region fallbacks to us-east and causing higher tail latency for eu/ap customers.
Immediate fix: rolled back gslb-weight-v2 at 2026-03-03T12:00Z (PR #1123). This restored geo-affinity and reduced latencies for affected customers.
Workaround provided to customer: region pinning header (X-Region-Preference) until fix was applied.

Follow-up actions: create INT-412 to run postmortem, add automated canary checks to detect geo-affinity regressions on rollout, add stricter rollout guardrail to prevent global weight changes without canary, and improve observability on upstream selection distribution.
Status: Mitigation complete, monitoring. Customer confirmed improved performance; ticket kept open for postmortem and follow-up tasks.
